bugs.summary: [Target Sources] A grouped review article with no stored review still counts as negative (tab, card, export)

description.description: A grouped review-page article whose pages hold no stored review is shown in the Negative perception tab as an empty row (title + URL line, no page block, no review, no passage) and is counted as a negative article in the tab, on the source card and in the export. The epic rule is that a page is negative only when it holds at least one negative review, so such an article must not count as negative (PO answer in GEO-1226, comment 873111).
steps_to_reproduce: Open staging, organisation QA-GEO, analysis Orange (16cdf040) > Action Center > Target Sources, period Last 30 days, LLMs ChatGPT + Gemini.
Open the panel of trustpilot.com (#5) and select the Negative perception tab.
Find the article ie.trustpilot.com/review/www.orange.ma (panel API: grouped = true, reviewCount = 0, pages = []).
Compare with the tab count, the source card and the XLSX export (Target Sources sheet, Failing articles).
description.expected_result: PO answer (GEO-1226 comment 873111): "If none of the pages of a grouped review article has a stored review, the article should NOT count as negative: not in the Negative perception tab, not on the card count and not in the export. [...] with no review there is no negative page and no negative article. We should not show the classic passage of a merged page either."
actual_result: The article ie.trustpilot.com/review/www.orange.ma is listed in the Negative perception tab with no page block, no review and no passage.
It is counted in "Negative perception (9)" and in the card count (9); the PDF / PPTX last page also shows "Negative perception in 9 articles" for trustpilot.com.
The XLSX export lists it in Failing articles with "Negative reviews" = 0 (row 193).
Same case for the grouped www.trustpilot.com/review/www.orange.fr article ("Read Customer Service Reviews of www.orange.fr") and for Toyota es.trustpilot.com/review/toyota.es.
